label: PROMPT: tricyclic as first-line
title: Tricyclic antidepressant as the first choice for depression
statement: Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) (e.g. amitriptyline, nortriptyline) should not be used as first-line in treatment of depression.

source.document: Cooper JA, et al. The development of the PROMPT criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484, Table 4
source.citation: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484
source.credit: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484

plain_summary: A tricyclic antidepressant such as amitriptyline or nortriptyline is not a good first choice for depression because it can cause dry mouth, constipation and drowsiness.

medicine_groups.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
medicine_groups.note: Low doses are often used for nerve pain, migraine or sleep. Those uses are not what the criterion is about. The reason for use comes from a condition line, not from the dose.

medicine_groups.name: Other antidepressants (shows an earlier antidepressant)
medicine_groups.note: Earlier use counts only when it was for depression.

rule_for_models: Check for first-line tricyclic treatment only at ages 45 to 64 inclusive (if age is missing, record eligibility as unknown and report no finding). Cite a tricyclic supply. Cite the line linking it to depression and the line giving the treatment order when present, including an answer that the order is unknown. Disregard earlier treatment documented solely for another reason. Unless the tricyclic was used solely for another reason or an earlier antidepressant was tried for depression, report a possible finding when either indication or the earlier treatment history is unclear and name the missing fact. If the reason is unclear, ask for Condition treated with this tricyclic. If use for depression is established and the treatment order is unclear, ask for First-line tricyclic antidepressant for depression. For the older question about whether another antidepressant was tried for depression before this tricyclic, No supports first-line use and Yes rules it out. An unknown answer leaves the order unclear.

needs_facts.meets: The record links this tricyclic to treatment of depression.

options.words: Depression, alone or along with another condition
Only a condition other than depression

needs_facts.meets: The tricyclic was the first antidepressant tried for depression. An earlier trial for depression rules out first-line use. If the treatment order is unknown, keep the finding possible when depression is established.

options.words: This tricyclic was the first antidepressant tried for depression
Another antidepressant was tried for depression before this tricyclic

cannot_be_seen: Why the tricyclic was started, what was tried before the start of this record, and the depression history. A short record cannot show that nothing was tried earlier. Also any supply from another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether a tricyclic antidepressant is the right first choice for this patient, or whether a different antidepressant could be used instead.
